messages:
maria-support: Hey team — customer hit a 401 (invalid_api_key) when calling /v1/embeddings. They say the same API key works for completions but fails for embeddings. Posting their curl they used and the response we received. Can someone help triage?

maria-support: curl --location --request POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings' \\
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...TRUNCATED...' \\
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  --data '{"model":"embed-lite-001","input":"test"}'

maria-support: Response: 401 {"error":{"message":"invalid_api_key","type":"authentication_error"}}

kevin-eng: thanks, leaving a note — two quick checks: 1) can you reproduce from our VPN (same region) to rule out edge rules, 2) any proxy/edge in front of the customer?

maria-support: repro from my laptop (no VPN) gets 401. I ran the exact same curl from our staging host (us-east) and it returns 200 with identical body/payload. Customer is behind a 3rd-party edge (FastEdge).

kevin-eng: interesting — that points to header mutation at the edge. @olivia-security do you want us to enable a short-lived debug log that prints a hashed fingerprint of the incoming Authorization header so we can compare what the edge forwarded vs what our origin saw? We will not log full keys.

olivia-security: ok with that for a narrow window. We must redact and hash first/last 6 chars only. Use HMAC-SHA256 with a per-run key. Make sure full logs are ephemeral (24h) and ACL'd to security + support. Approve for a 30-min window.

kevin-eng: deployed a tiny patch behind feature-flag to log this:
```
// redacted snippet
const auth = req.headers['authorization'] || ''
const fingerprint = hashWithHmac(auth).slice(0,12)
logger.info('auth-fingerprint', { fingerprint })
```
Logging enabled for request ids matching Acme-Tenant.

support-bot: Deploy succeeded: flag=auth-fingerprint enabled for tenant=acme, window=30m :white_check_mark:

maria-support: After enabling, we see two different fingerprints: request from customer edge -> fingerprint=A1B2C3D4E5F6, same curl from staging -> fingerprint=ZZYYXX001122. They do not match.

kevin-eng: can you ask the customer to paste the header value exactly (redacted) they send? specifically check for stray characters around the token (leading/trailing whitespace, extra punctuation). Also ask them to run `curl -v` to show the raw request header.

maria-support: Customer pasted back: 'Authorization: Bearer .sk_live_ABCDEF...' — they accidentally have a leading dot before the key. They say one of their devs concatenates the token with a dot as a joiner in their mobile SDK when a config value is missing.

kevin-eng: that explains it — the leading '.' changes the token string and fails validation so we produce invalid_api_key. Edge forwarded the header unchanged; our origin saw it and rejected. The reason completions worked earlier is they were using a different internal svc that strips punctuation before calling (ugh).

oncall-dan: Recommend we add a defensive normalization step in the gateway that strips accidental leading/trailing punctuation around bearer tokens and emits a distinct metric for malformed-token requests. Will file a follow-up PR but we should not silently accept arbitrary mutations — only strip common paste mistakes (leading/trailing '.' or '"' or '\\n').

olivia-security: agree on metric + opt-in normalization controlled by a runtime flag, and only for a short grace period. Make sure to monitor for abuse.

maria-support: Customer applied the fix on their side (removed the leading dot) and confirmed embedding request now returns 200. They patched their mobile SDK to avoid concatenating with '.' when config missing.

maria-support: Closing this ticket as resolved, root cause = client-side accidental leading character (.) in Authorization header produced malformed token -> 401 invalid_api_key. Notes: enabled fingerprint logs for 30m, no sensitive data stored, follow-up: kevin to open PR for optional normalization + metric.

kevin-eng: PR filed: #1792 — adds opt-in normalize_bearer_tokens flag + metric guard.

olivia-security: closing ack. :lock:
